meta.title: Corporate Laptop Cannot Connect to Network
meta.description: Level 1/2 IT helpdesk: a finance analyst's laptop can't reach the intranet or the internet after a VPN client update. Talk to the customer, diagnose with real Windows networking commands, fix the root cause, validate and document.
meta.briefing: You are on the Service Desk at Northwind Corp. Ticket INC0042317 has just been assigned to you: Priya Shah in Finance can't reach the intranet or any websites from her laptop. She is waiting on Teams chat and has a month-end deadline. You have remote PowerShell access to her laptop, the knowledge base and the directory admin console. Diagnose, fix, validate and close the ticket professionally.
objectives: Gather a clear problem history from the customer
Isolate the fault with layered network diagnostics
Identify and fix the root cause with the least disruption
Validate the fix technically and with the customer
Document the resolution and close the ticket

actions.label: Read KB-0988: GlobalConnect VPN 5.2 known issues

outputs.text:
**KB-0988 · GlobalConnect VPN 5.2.x: known issues**

*Symptom:* after the automatic upgrade to 5.2.0/5.2.1 some laptops cannot resolve internal or external names while in the office. Ping by IP address works.

*Cause:* the installer migrates the legacy split-tunnel profile and leaves the decommissioned DNS server 10.0.0.53/10.0.0.54 configured **statically** on the physical adapter.

*Resolution:* set the adapter's DNS to obtain automatically (DHCP), e.g. `Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceAlias <adapter> -ResetServerAddresses`, then `ipconfig /flushdns` and verify with `nslookup`. Do **not** reinstall drivers or reset the TCP/IP stack; neither removes the setting.

**KB-1043 · DNS troubleshooting checklist**

1. `ipconfig /all`: confirm IP, gateway and DNS servers (corporate DNS: 10.20.1.10 and 10.20.1.11, assigned by DHCP).
2. `ping` the gateway and a public IP (8.8.8.8) to prove IP connectivity.
3. `ping`/`nslookup` a name. If IP works but names fail, it's DNS.
4. `nslookup <name> 10.20.1.10` to test the corporate server directly.
5. Fix the client configuration, `ipconfig /flushdns`, re-test, confirm with the user, document.

**KB-0201 · Password reset**

Verify identity, reset in Directory Admin, force change at next logon. Resets sign the user out of every device.

**KB-0750 · Wireless driver reinstall**

Only when Device Manager reports an error code or the adapter cannot associate. Takes 15-25 minutes.

feedback_rules.text: You gathered a clear problem history (symptoms, timing and recent changes) before touching the system.
You isolated the fault to name resolution by contrasting ping-by-IP with name lookups.
Querying the corporate DNS server directly was an expert move: it proved the servers were healthy and the client was misconfigured.
You checked the knowledge base and found the known VPN 5.2 issue.
You validated the fix technically and with the customer before closing.
Your resolution notes captured cause, fix and verification.
Ask whether other devices or colleagues are affected to scope the incident (one device vs. the whole site).
Always ask what changed recently. The VPN update was the key clue.
Reinstalling the driver wasted 20 minutes; the adapter was up and ping by IP proved the driver was fine.
Resetting the password disrupted the user without any evidence of an account problem.
Avoid 'shotgun' fixes like netsh resets. Diagnose first, then make the smallest change that addresses the cause.
Never point corporate devices at public DNS. Internal names won't resolve and security filtering is bypassed.
Hard-coding the corporate DNS servers works, but resetting to DHCP is more robust.
The customer escalated because the incident dragged on. Communicate progress and avoid disruptive steps.
Record a diagnosis only when the evidence supports it.
Flush the DNS resolver cache (ipconfig /flushdns) after changing DNS servers.
Validate technically after the fix (nslookup intranet.corp.local or Test-NetConnection).
Ask the customer to confirm the fix from her side before closing.
Write resolution notes: symptoms, root cause, fix and verification.
The root cause, a stale static DNS server left by the VPN client update, was never fixed. Resetting the adapter's DNS to DHCP resolves it.
Briefly explaining the cause in plain language builds trust and reduces repeat calls.
